name: Extension
summary: Extension, the melanocortin 1 receptor (MC1R), also called red factor: whether the horse can make black pigment at all. One working copy, E, is enough: the horse is black, bay or another black-based colour, as agouti decides. Two recessive copies - e, the common red allele, or the rarer ea, in any combination - leave only red pigment in the coat, a chestnut (sorrel), and hide the agouti genotype, which is still passed on. Skin and eyes keep their pigment: a chestnut can have dark skin and dark eyes. Both red alleles are single-base changes in exon 1, two bases apart: e is c.248C>T (g.36979560C>T on chromosome 3, EquCab3.0; older papers call it C901T) and ea is c.250G>A (g.36979562G>A). A test that looks only at the e site can miss ea. An E/E horse cannot have a chestnut foal. The red allele e was found in all 28 breeds of one large survey; ea was found in the Knabstrupper, Paint Horse, Percheron and Quarter Horse, and is reported particularly in Belgian Draft horses. e is described as common in Haflingers, Suffolks, Belgians, many pony breeds and some gaited breeds, and ea as much rarer; no per-breed figure was given. Blood bay, liver bay and seal brown are shades or looks of black-based horses, not alleles of this locus; no dosage effect of E is established - an E/E bay is not reliably darker than an E/e bay, and such differences are put down to polygenic shade, sooty, nutrition, season and age. No effect on build or performance is established.

phenotypes.name: Wild type
phenotypes.description: At least one E. Black pigment can be made; whether it covers the body or only the points is agouti's business.

phenotypes.name: Chestnut
phenotypes.description: Two recessive red alleles, e or ea in any combination. No black pigment in the coat: the horse is chestnut (sorrel) with a red mane and tail, whatever its agouti genotype.

frequencies.population: Pony of the Americas (allele frequency of e 0.76, relatedness-filtered, Avila et al. 2022; genotype shares worked out from it assuming random mating)
